security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD's RISC-V context switch (cpu_switch in swtch.S:258) and bhyve VCPU switch (vmmops_vcpu_save_csrs/vmmops_vcpu_restore_csrs in vmm_riscv.c:161-195) save/restore neither siselect/sireg* nor vsiselect/vsireg* across thread or VM boundaries. If Smcsrind/Sscsrind is implemented in hardware, a thread or guest VM that writes to siselect/vsiselect can have its indirect CSR window state silently inherited by the next scheduled thread or VM, which then reads/writes a different CSR than intended via sireg*/vsireg* because the select register was not sanitized on context switch. Additionally, the hypcsr struct (riscv.h:56-68) has no fields for vsiselect/vsireg*, so bhyve cannot virtualize this extension at all, leaving guest accesses to these CSRs with UNSPECIFIED behavior per the spec.
security_spec.summary: siselect/sireg* and vsiselect/vsireg* CSR state not saved/restored on context switch or VM entry/exit, leaking indirect CSR window configuration between threads and across VM boundaries

findings.finding: struct pcb has no fields for siselect or sireg* (indirect CSR access registers). When Smcsrind/Sscsrind is implemented in hardware, there is no storage to save/restore these per-thread CSR window registers across context switches. A thread that writes to siselect to alias sireg* to a specific CSR will have its indirection state silently inherited by the next scheduled thread.
findings.snippet:
struct pcb {
  uint64_t pcb_ra;       /* Return address */
  uint64_t pcb_sp;       /* Stack pointer */
  uint64_t pcb_gp;       /* Global pointer */
  uint64_t pcb_tp;       /* Thread pointer */
  uint64_t pcb_s[12];    /* Saved registers */

findings.finding: cpu_switch saves/restores ra, sp, s0-s11, and conditionally FPU state, but does NOT save/restore siselect or sireg* CSRs. If Smcsrind/Sscsrind is implemented, the indirect CSR alias window (set by the previous thread via siselect) persists across the context switch. The new thread will read/write a different CSR than intended when accessing sireg*, constituting a cross-thread information leak via CSR aliasing.
findings.snippet:
ENTRY(cpu_switch)
  sd a1, PC_CURTHREAD(tp)
  ld x13, TD_PCB(a1)
  sd x13, PC_CURPCB(tp)
  ld x13, TD_PCB(a0)
  sd ra, (PCB_RA)(x13)

findings.finding: cpu_throw (used when a new thread starts for the first time) does not initialize siselect or sireg* to known-safe values. A new thread inherits whatever indirection state was left in the hardware CSRs by the previous thread, creating the same CSR aliasing leak as cpu_switch.
findings.snippet:
ENTRY(cpu_throw)
  mv s0, a1
  mv a0, a1
  call _C_LABEL(pmap_activate_sw)
  mv a0, s0
  sd a0, PC_CURTHREAD(tp)

findings.finding: struct hypcsr has no fields for vsiselect or vsireg*. bhyve therefore has no storage capacity to virtualize the Sscsrind extension for guest VMs. Guest accesses to vsiselect/vsireg* will have UNSPECIFIED behavior per the RISC-V privileged spec — they may trap to M-mode, silently alias to the host's indirection state, or produce undefined results. This is a structural gap in bhyve's CSR virtualization that cannot be fixed without adding fields to this struct.

vmmops_vcpu_save_csrs reads and saves vsstatus, vsie, vstvec, vsscratch, vsepc, vscause, vstval, hvip, and vsatp, but does NOT read or save vsiselect or vsireg*. On VM exit, the guest's indirect CSR indirection state is silently discarded, so any guest that uses Smcsrind/Sscsrind loses its CSR window configuration across VM exits.

vmmops_vcpu_restore_csrs writes vsstatus, vsie, vstvec, vsscratch, vsepc, vscause, vstval, hvip, and vsatp from the saved struct, but does NOT write vsiselect or vsireg*. On VM entry, the guest's indirect CSR alias state is not restored. If the host kernel or another VM has modified siselect, that stale indirection state leaks into the guest VM's CSR window on entry.

vmm_switch performs the low-level world-switch (GPR save/restore + sstatus/hstatus/scounteren/sscratch/stvec swap) between host and guest. It does not touch siselect/vsiselect or sireg*/vsireg* at all. The indirection state is implicitly shared between host and guest across sret/mret transitions.
findings.snippet:
ENTRY(vmm_switch)
  sd ra, (HYP_H_RA)(a0)
  sd sp, (HYP_H_SP)(a0)
  sd tp, (HYP_H_TP)(a0)
  sd gp, (HYP_H_GP)(a0)
  sd s0, (HYP_H_S + 0 * 8)(a0)

findings.finding: vmmops_init allocates and zeroes the hyp struct. Not directly related to the Smcsrind/Sscsrind vulnerability. The initialization itself is correct for the current code, but the hyp structure it creates (struct hyp, which contains hypctx with hypcsr) lacks vsiselect/vsireg* fields.

vmmops_run is the main VCPU execution loop. It calls vmmops_vcpu_restore_csrs before the guest runs and vmmops_vcpu_save_csrs after VM exit. Since neither function handles vsiselect/vsireg*, the guest's indirect CSR state is not properly virtualized across the run loop boundary. Furthermore, the host kernel code between VM exits may itself use siselect/sireg, overwriting any guest state.

savectx saves GPRs and FPU state for CPU suspend/hibernate, but does not save siselect or sireg*. Same structural gap as cpu_switch — if the CPU is suspended and resumed, the indirection state is lost.
findings.snippet:
ENTRY(savectx)
  sd ra, (PCB_RA)(a0)
  sd sp, (PCB_SP)(a0)
  sd tp, (PCB_TP)(a0)
  sd gp, (PCB_GP)(a0)
  sd s0, (PCB_S + 0 * 8)(a0)
